title: The Sega/Yamaha AICA register map
covers: the AICA registers as MAME's device handles them: the slot words that change derived state, the global control, timer, interrupt and DMA words, and the DSP banks; no official document was found

searched.gave: The header of aica.cpp names the part as Sega/Yamaha 315-6232, earlier 315-6119, and cites no document.
A web search gave Sega's Dreamcast Hardware Specification Outline, a block description with no register model, and no Yamaha AICA manual.
The components listing has no Sega folder, and the Yamaha folder holds no AICA document.
A search found Sega's Dreamcast Hardware Specification Outline (Rev.0819), whose AICA chapter gives no register-level model, and game manuals only.
datasheetarchive.com answered 315-6232 with unrelated connectors and fuses, and no AICA document.

rows.text: Word 0 holds KEYONEX in bit 15, KEYONB in bit 14, SSCTL in bit 10, LPCTL in bit 9, PCMS in bits 8-7, and address bits 22-16 in bits 6-0.
A write stores the word; with bit 15 set it starts released slots holding bit 14 and releases slots without it, then clears bit 15.
Slot word 0x18 holds the octave in bits 14-11 and the frequency number in bits 9-0.
A write stores the word and recomputes the slot's pitch step from the octave and the frequency number.
Slot word 0x14 holds the release rate in bits 4-0, the decay level in bits 9-5, the key rate scaling in bits 13-10 and the loop-start link in bit 14.
A write stores the word and recomputes the envelope's release rate and decay level from those fields.
Word 0x1C holds LFORE in bit 15, the LFO frequency in bits 14-10, the phase waveform and depth in bits 9-5, and the amplitude pair in bits 4-0.
A write stores the word and recomputes the LFO steps whose depth field is not zero.
Slot word 0x24 holds the direct send level in bits 11-8 and the direct pan in bits 4-0, read as 0 when mono is set.
A write stores the word; the slot handler changes nothing, and the mixer reads the level and pan when it sounds the slot.
Offset 0x04 holds the ring-buffer size in bits 14-13, one of four sizes in kwords, and the ring-buffer pointer in bits 11-0.
A write stores the word and sets the DSP ring buffer to 8, 16, 32 or 64 kwords from bits 14-13, its pointer from bits 11-0.
Offset 0x08 is the MIDI input register; the handler takes the word's low byte as a received byte.
A write queues the word's low byte in a sixteen-byte stack, advancing the write index modulo sixteen.
A read returns the stack byte at the read index in bits 7-0, cancels the sound IRQ, and advances the index when the stack is not empty.
Offsets 0x12 to 0x17 have no write handler of their own: the update switch only breaks for them.
A write stores the word at its offset; the update handler changes nothing else.
Offset 0x80 supplies bits 22-16 of the DMA destination address from its bits 9-15; offset 0x84 supplies the low bits.
A write stores the word and replaces bits 22-16 of the DMA destination address from bits 9-15, keeping its low bits.
Offset 0x84 supplies bits 15-2 of the DMA destination address; its bits 1-0 are ignored.
A write stores the word and replaces bits 15-2 of the DMA destination address, keeping bits 22-16.
Offset 0x88 holds the DMA source address in bits 14-2 and the DMA gate in bit 15.
A write stores the word, sets the DMA source address from bits 14-2 and the gate from bit 15.
Offset 0x8C holds the DMA length in bits 14-2, the direction in bit 15 and the execute bit 0.
A write stores the word and, when bit 0 is set, runs the DMA transfer immediately.
With the direction set and the gate bit set, the transfer writes zeros to two bytes per step, then clears bit 0 and sets pending bit 4.
Offset 0x90 holds timer A's prescaler in bits 10-8 as a power of two and its count in bits 7-0.
A write stores the word and, with an IRQ handler bound, sets timer A's period from the prescaler and count; a count of 0xFF starts none.
On expiry the counter becomes 0xFFFF, pending bit 6 is set and the count's high byte is written to bits 7-0.
Offset 0x94 holds timer B's prescaler in bits 10-8 as a power of two and its count in bits 7-0.
A write stores the word and, with an IRQ handler bound, sets timer B's period from the prescaler and count; a count of 0xFF starts none.
On expiry the counter becomes 0xFFFF, pending bit 7 is set and the count's high byte is written to bits 7-0.
Offset 0x98 holds timer C's prescaler in bits 10-8 as a power of two and its count in bits 7-0.
A write stores the word and, with an IRQ handler bound, sets timer C's period from the prescaler and count; a count of 0xFF starts none.
On expiry the counter becomes 0xFFFF, pending bit 8 is set and the count's high byte is written to bits 7-0.
Offset 0x9C is the SCI interrupt enable mask; bits 6-8 enable the timer interrupts, and the MIDI stack raises its own.
A write stores the word and logs a request for help when any of bits 0, 4, 5, 9 or 10 is set.
Offset 0xA4 is the SCI interrupt reset register: a 1 in a bit clears that source's pending interrupt.
A write, with an IRQ handler bound, clears the pending bits it sets, then sets again the bits of expired timers.
Offsets 0xA8, 0xAC and 0xB0 are the three SCI level registers: each source's level takes one bit from each, in order.
A write to any of the three recomputes the levels of timer A, timers B and C, and MIDI, when an IRQ handler is bound.
Offset 0xB4 is the main SH-4 interrupt enable mask; a write with any of bits 0-4 or 6-10 set logs a request for help.
A write stores the word as the main enable mask and recomputes the SH-4 interrupt line.
The line is raised when the pending and enable masks intersect and lowered when they do not.
Offset 0xB8 is the main interrupt pending register: a write with bit 5 set sets pending bit 5, and a read returns the mask.
A write whose bit 5 is set sets pending bit 5, then recomputes the SH-4 interrupt line.
Offset 0xBC is the main interrupt reset: a write clears from the pending mask every bit it sets.
A write clears those bits from the pending mask and recomputes the SH-4 interrupt line.
Offset 0x10 is a slot monitor: the MSLC field of register 0x0C, bits 13-8, picks the slot, and AFSEL in bit 14 picks the view.
Read with AFSEL clear, it returns the loop flag in bit 15, the envelope phase in bits 14-13 and the inverted volume in bits 12-3, and clears the flag.
Read with AFSEL set, it returns only bit 15; a TODO asks whether the envelope should be monitored too.
Offset 0x14 is the current-address monitor of the slot named by MSLC, register 0x0C bits 13-8.
A read returns the slot's play address with its twelve fraction bits dropped, whatever the sample format.
0x2000 to 0x2044 are the effect table: each word holds the send level in bits 11-8 and the pan in bits 4-0, by slot index.
A write stores the word at index (addr&0x7F)>>2 up to 0x2044; a write above it is ignored.
The mixer applies the table's send level and pan to the DSP's sixteen effect returns and to the two external inputs.
0x2D00 is the interrupt level register: a write stores it with a warning, and a read returns it.
A write stores the level and logs a warning.
A read returns the stored level.
0x2D04 holds the interrupt request word; a read returns it.
A write stores the word, clears the sound IRQ when bit 0 is set, and logs a warning for bit 8 or any other bit.
0x3000 to 0x31FF are the DSP coefficient RAM, 256 words at index (addr-0x3000)/2.
A write stores the word in the coefficient array at that index.
A read returns the word held at that index.
0x3200 to 0x32FF are the DSP MAD offset table, 128 words at index (addr-0x3200)/2.
A write stores the word in the offset table at that index.
A read returns the word held at that index.
0x3400 to 0x3BFF are the DSP microprogram, 1024 words at index (addr-0x3400)/2.
A write stores the word; a write to 0x3BFE, the last word, also starts the DSP.
A read returns the stored word.
0x4000 to 0x43FF are the 128 DSP TEMP registers, 32-bit, at index (addr>>3)&0x7F; bit 2 picks the low or high half.
A write replaces one 16-bit half of the register its address picks.
A read returns the half its address picks.
0x4400 to 0x44FF are the 32 DSP MEMS registers, 32-bit, at index (addr>>3)&0x1F; bit 2 picks the low or high half.
A write replaces one 16-bit half of the register its address picks.
A read returns the half its address picks.
0x4500 to 0x457F are the 16 DSP MIXS registers, 32-bit, at index (addr>>3)&0xF; bit 2 picks the low or high half.
A write replaces one 16-bit half of the register its address picks.
A read returns the half its address picks.
0x4580 to 0x45BF are the sixteen effect return registers, one per four bytes at (addr-0x4580)/4.
A write stores the word in the effect return register its address picks.
A read returns the word held at that index.
0x45C0 is the base of the DSP's two external audio inputs, 16-bit signed.
A read indexes EXTS by (addr-0x45C0)/2 below 0x45C8, so 0x45C4 and 0x45C6 read past the two-word array.
A write is not stored: the write path is commented out.
